messages.author: 08f3062efe0fd1ca
messages.subject: scale_x_discrete and line breaks
parts:
Hello List,

I noticed an interesting feature. Consider the following minimal reproducible example:

ac <- structure(list(treatment = structure(c(3L, 1L, 8L, 8L, 3L, 3L,
                                3L, 6L, 1L, 7L, 3L, 8L, 8L, 2L, 6L, 3L, 4L, 7L, 4L, 1L, 6L, 8L,
                                3L, 6L, 5L, 3L, 7L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 4L, 3L, 3L, 8L, 5L, 5L, 3L, 5L,
                                8L, 4L, 7L, 5L, 3L, 3L, 5L, 6L, 3L, 5L, 2L, 8L), .Label = c("auniFCS",
                                "bunilateral.FCSAc", "cFCStwicedur", "FCSFCSAcdelayedhalf", "FCSFCSAcdelayedonce",
                                "FCSFCSAcdelayhalfinterval", "FCSFCSAcoverlapping", "zuniFCShalfint"
                        ), class = "factor"), finalindex = c(0.80184725, 0.446666667,
                        0.609157803, 0.642514362, 0.662789312, 0.513333333, 0.748459489,
                        0.555379517, 0.713303805, 0.800691333, 0.604661811, 0.411343748,
                        0.393496469, 0.366666667, 0.634095511, 0.845563667, 0.388888889,
                        0.801910825, 0.660128878, 0.770948464, 0.311111111, 0.316666667,
                        0.639943228, 0.622600347, 0.774008892, 0.513333333, 0.760470465,
                        0.513333333, 0.446666667, 0.719091026, 0.578640636, 0.694069341,
                        0.80744682, 0.497962435, 0.791408043, 0.769137923, 0.818978214,
                        0.646995255, 0.316666667, 0.587870292, 0.7990585, 0.7756245,
                        0.513333333, 0.746923099, 0.712100736, 0.644444027, 0.771631975,
                        0.479166667, 0.366666667, 0.316666667)), .Names = c("treatment",
                "finalindex"), row.names = c(268L, 153L, 189L, 188L, 229L, 276L,
                273L, 13L, 131L, 106L, 262L, 197L, 203L, 222L, 58L, 264L, 92L,
                121L, 66L, 158L, 4L, 194L, 233L, 67L, 51L, 251L, 118L, 237L,
                157L, 161L, 76L, 254L, 265L, 169L, 93L, 44L, 263L, 48L, 198L,
                41L, 111L, 74L, 248L, 270L, 36L, 23L, 275L, 87L, 214L, 196L), class = "data.frame")

Plotting:

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(ac, aes(y=finalindex, x=treatment))
p + geom_boxplot() + scale_x_discrete("Treatment")

Because labels overlap, I try breaking them with \n:

p + geom_boxplot() +
        scale_x_discrete("Treatment", labels=(c("unilateral \n FCS",
                                    "unilateral \n FCSAc",
                                    "unilateral \n long FCS",
                                    "overlapping",
                                    "half \n delayed",
                                    "once \n delayed",
                                    "alternating",
                                    "unilateral \n FCSfast")))

And this is the error that is produced as a result:
Error: Labels can only be specified in conjunction with breaks

When I introduce breaks, things are back to normal:

p + geom_boxplot() +
        scale_x_discrete("Treatment", labels=(c("unilateral \n FCS",
                                    "unilateral \n FCSAc",
                                    "unilateral \n long FCS",
                                    "overlapping",
                                    "half \n delayed",
                                    "once \n delayed",
                                    "alternating",
                                    "unilateral \n FCSfast")),
                breaks=levels(ac$treatment))

I'm curious, is this a desired ("normal") behavior when introducing line breaks?

Cheers from Slovenia,
Roman

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_discrete and line breaks
parts:
p + geom_boxplot() + coord_flip()

or
p + geom_boxplot() + opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))

You can save a little space by removing the x-axis label and perhaps reducing
the size of the font a bit.

HTH,
Dennis
